summary: Cleveland NF, San Diego County, CA 7x7-ft ground cab built 1912 by Ed Bish; listed abandoned by 1938, lost to fire in the 1950s; concrete foundation remains per register.

facts.design: 7x7-ft wood ground-mounted cab with a hip roof, reached by a 29-ft ladder up the granite summit
facts.status_note: Cab no longer stands; the 7x7 concrete foundation remains per the register and FFLA-SDRC. Peakbagging says nothing remains today.
facts.agency: City of Escondido, California (per register; a 2013 county ownership is reported by Lerner)

access.note: Site lies in a 418-acre County of San Diego open space preserve; no source describes the preserve's visitor rules

visit.trail_note: A hike to the summit; Lerner describes a group climb as strenuous. The Times-Advocate article places the trailhead near a dirt parking lot off Oakvale Road near Lake Wohlford Road in Valley Center, and warns that the path is uneven and poison oak is common.

corrections.why: FFLA-SDRC gives 2136 ft/651 m and Peakbagging gives 2136 ft; the register's 1,725 ft (526 m) is paired with coordinates given to whole seconds (117 00 00 W). Lerner also places the slab at 2,083 ft, with 2,136 ft including the hip roof. The editor should decide which figure to keep.

corrections.proposed: County of San Diego (open space preserve owner since 2013), with the City of Escondido noted as the register's administrator
corrections.why: The register (2009 registration) names the City of Escondido; the Valley Center history article says the County of San Diego has owned the 418-acre preserve since 2013. The editor should check county records before changing the field.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FFLA-SDRC spell the ranger Bish; the 1912 Los Angeles Times report, as quoted, spells it Bush. The story uses Bish and notes the 1912 spelling.
The register and Lerner place the abandoned listing at a 1938 data sheet (by 1938); Peakbagging says by 1937. The story gives 1938 as the source year and notes Peakbagging's date.

The register, FFLA-SDRC and Lerner say the concrete foundation or slab still exists; Peakbagging says nothing remains today, though it also mentions concrete steps. The story reports the disagreement.

The register gives 1,725 ft; FFLA-SDRC and Peakbagging give 2136 ft; the 1912 report gives 2106 ft above sea level; Lerner gives 2,083 ft for the slab and 2,136 ft with the hip roof. The story says the figures vary.
The register (2009) names the City of Escondido; Lerner says the County of San Diego has owned the preserve since 2013. Both are reported.

sources.title: Climbers make trek to historic peak

notes_for_editor: Built year (1912), Ed Bish as ranger and the 29-ft ladder are consistent across the register and FFLA-SDRC. Sources conflict on elevation (1,725 ft vs 2,136 ft), abandonment year (1937 vs 1938), foundation today, and administering agency (City of Escondido in a 2009 register vs County of San Diego owner since 2013). Two corrections are proposed for the editor; neither is applied. The 1912 newspaper text is quoted on a fan site (californialookouts.weebly.com) rather than the original paper, so the Bush spelling is secondhand. The Valley Center article is dated October 31, 2019. The register's 'Removed' and 'Administered by' fields are the only register evidence for the agency. Access is recorded as public because the land is an open space preserve, and the article mentions a county management plan but gives no visitor rules.
